root_cause_label: Misunderstood pickup/drop mechanics: actions apply to current cell not adjacent
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent persistently issued pickup and drop actions based on adjacent cell conditions, but the game engine only applies those actions to the player's current cell, so no blocks were ever successfully collected or placed and the stair-building loop ran forever without winning.
t_err_evidence: cat <<'EOF' > /app/solution.js — writes solution using pickup/drop on adjacent cells, wrong API usage
t_commit_evidence: Step 4: the broken adjacent-cell pickup/drop pattern is written into solution.js and never corrected across all subsequent rewrites (steps 5, 9, 10, 11, 12, 15, 18, 19, 21, 23); the agent replaces one broken variant with another broken variant every iteration, locking in the failing outcome.
t_surface_evidence: DEBUG: invoking game.run(3) — test hangs, no results produced, trials never complete
trigger_explanation: The agent read challenge.js (step 3) but did not correctly understand that c.pickup() and c.drop() in the game engine operate on n[u.y][u.x] (the player's current cell). It instead assumed pickup/drop could be triggered by adjacent cell conditions, a fundamental misreading of the API contract that produced a solution that never successfully manipulates any block.
